subject: General Knowledge
description: Covers Garba and Rouf folk dances.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an energetic and vibrant folk dance of Gujarat, traditionally performed during the nine nights of the Navratri festival?

options.option_text: Garba
Bihu
Lavani
Ghoomar

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Garba is the iconic folk dance of Gujarat. It is traditionally performed by women (and increasingly men) in a circle around a centrally lit clay lantern (Garbha Deep) or an image of the Goddess Amba. The circular movement symbolizes the cycle of time (birth, life, death, rebirth), while the goddess in the center remains the only constant, unchanging reality. It is deeply associated with the Navratri festival.
DECOY BUSTING: Bihu is the harvest dance of Assam. Lavani is a powerful, rhythmic dance of Maharashtra, heavily associated with the dholki drum. Ghoomar is the traditional folk dance of the Bhil tribe (and later Rajputs) in Rajasthan.
EXAM INSIGHT: In December 2023, Garba of Gujarat was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, making it a highly probable current affairs/static GK question.

questions.stem: Rouf is a traditional and highly rhythmic folk dance performed mainly by women to celebrate the arrival of spring. It originates from which region?

options.option_text: Jammu & Kashmir
Punjab
Himachal Pradesh
Uttarakhand

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Rouf (pronounced Rof) is one of the most popular traditional folk dances of the Kashmir Valley. It is performed exclusively by women during the spring season and major festivals like Eid and Ramzan. The dancers form two rows facing each other, link their arms, and sway backward and forward in a rhythmic motion while singing traditional Kashmiri poetry (Chakri).
DECOY BUSTING: Punjab is famous for Bhangra (men) and Giddha (women). Himachal Pradesh is famous for Nati (which holds the Guinness record for the largest folk dance). Uttarakhand is known for Choliya (a martial sword dance).
EXAM INSIGHT: Folk dances are highly repeated in SSC and Railway exams. Key pairings to memorize: Tarangamel (Goa), Kalbelia (Rajasthan - snake charmers), Yakshagana (Karnataka), and Cheraw (Mizoram - bamboo dance).

questions.stem: The Dollu Kunitha folk dance of Karnataka, performed with large barrel-shaped drums, is traditionally associated with which community?

options.option_text: Kuruba shepherd community of Karnataka
Kodava warrior community of the Coorg region
Lingayat farming community of northern Karnataka
Vokkaliga cultivator community of Old Mysore

questions.explanation: Dollu Kunitha is performed by the Kuruba (shepherd) community of Karnataka. 'Dollu' means drum; the vigorous percussive dance is central to Kuruba identity. Kodava and Vokkaliga are major Karnataka communities but have their own distinct forms (Kailpodhu and Kolata respectively). Lingayats perform Veeragase during festivals, not Dollu Kunitha.

questions.stem: The Panthi folk dance of Chhattisgarh is a devotional performance associated with the birth anniversary of which spiritual figure?

options.option_text: Kabir Das, the 15th-century poet-saint of Varanasi
Guru Baba Ghasi Das, founder of the Satnami community
Sant Ravidas, the Bhakti movement cobbler-saint
Guru Ghasidas Mahant, reformer of the Baiga tribe

questions.explanation: Panthi is the devotional folk dance of the Satnami community of Chhattisgarh, performed specifically on Maghi Purnima — the birth anniversary of Guru Baba Ghasi Das. The Satnamis drew inspiration from Kabir's teachings (making option A tempting), but Panthi is distinctly linked to Ghasi Das. Ravidas and the Baiga tribe have no connection to this dance tradition.

questions.stem: The name 'Ghoomar', Rajasthan's traditional circular folk dance, is etymologically derived from which core element of the performance?

options.option_text: The 'ghunghroo' ankle bells tied to the feet of every dancer
The 'ghooma' spinning whirl executed in a circular formation
The 'ghoonghat' veil that dancers dramatically adjust mid-performance
The 'ghada' earthen pot balanced atop the dancer's head

questions.explanation: Ghoomar derives from 'ghooma' (to whirl or spin in Rajasthani). The signature movement is a circular spinning turn under a voluminous ghagra skirt that creates a bell-shaped swirl. Ghunghroo (ankle bells) appear in many dances and are not the naming root. The ghoonghat is worn but is not etymological. Ghada-balancing on the head is the hallmark of Bhawai, a separate Rajasthani form.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of folk dance and its associated performing community is CORRECTLY matched?

options.option_text: Kalbelia dance — Bhil tribal community of Rajasthan
Teratali dance — Kamad community of Rajasthan
Bhavai dance — Kathiawadi fishing community of Gujarat
Nati dance — Gaddi shepherd community of Himachal Pradesh

questions.explanation: Teratali is performed by women of the Kamad community of Rajasthan, who attach manjiras (small cymbals) to their knees and body and strike them rhythmically while seated — a distinctive form. Kalbelia belongs to the Kalbelia snake-charmer caste, not the Bhil. Bhavai is a Gujarati theatrical form associated with the Nayak/Thakar community, not Kathiawadi fishermen. Nati is broadly Himachali (Kullu valley) and not specific to the Gaddi pastoralists.

questions.stem: Which of the following folk dances does NOT originate from a northeastern state of India?

options.option_text: Cheraw — bamboo pole folk dance of Mizoram
Nongkrem — Khasi community festival dance of Meghalaya
Wangala — Garo harvest festival dance of Meghalaya
Karma — Oraon and Munda tribal dance of Jharkhand

questions.explanation: Karma dance is performed by the Oraon, Munda, and Ho tribes of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha — central India, not the northeast. The name derives from the Karam tree, worshipped during the Karma festival. Cheraw (Mizoram), Nongkrem (Meghalaya–Khasi), and Wangala (Meghalaya–Garo) are all authentically northeastern. Candidates commonly conflate tribal dances of central India with northeastern tribal traditions.

questions.stem: In Odisha's Gotipua tradition — widely considered a precursor to classical Odissi — adolescent boys perform devotional items dressed as women. The term 'Gotipua' literally translates to:

options.option_text: 'Temple devotee' — from goti (sacred grove) and pua (ritual offering)
'Single boy' — from goti (one/single) and pua (boy in Odia)
'Nimble dancer' — denoting acrobatic mastery achieved through early training
'Solitary singer' — referring to performance without instrumental accompaniment

questions.explanation: In Odia, 'goti' means one or single and 'pua' means boy or son, so Gotipua = 'single boy' (solo male performer). These pre-pubescent boys train in solo items combining Odissi movements with acrobatics and devotional content dedicated to Lord Jagannath. The 'temple devotee' etymology is a plausible but incorrect folk reading; the term actually describes the gender-and-number identity of the performer, not their ritual status.

questions.stem: Theyyam, the ritualistic performance of Kerala where the performer is believed to embody the deity during the ritual, is concentrated in which geographical sub-region of the state?

options.option_text: South Kerala — Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam districts
Central Kerala — Thrissur and Palakkad districts
North Kerala — Kannur and Kasaragod districts
Mid-Malabar — Kozhikode and Malappuram districts

questions.explanation: Theyyam is endemic to North Kerala (northern Malabar), centred on Kannur (Cannanore) and Kasaragod districts. It is performed at kavu (sacred groves) by communities such as Malayan, Vannan, and Velan who embody ancestral spirits and deities. Kozhikode and Malappuram are also Malabar districts and form a tempting distractor, but the core Theyyam belt is specifically the northernmost zone. Thrissur and Travancore districts have entirely different ritual performance traditions.

questions.stem: Lavani, a folk dance-drama known for its powerful rhythm and expressive lyrics, is the traditional performing art of which state?

options.option_text: Karnataka, known for the Dollu Kunitha drum dance form
Madhya Pradesh, known for the Karma tribal ritual dance
Andhra Pradesh, home to the Perini Sivatandavam style
Maharashtra, performed to the rhythmic beats of Dholki

questions.explanation: Lavani is Maharashtra's celebrated folk dance-drama, performed by women artists (often in Tamasha troupes) to the fast beats of the Dholki barrel drum. Karnataka's signature drum-dance is Dollu Kunitha. Perini Sivatandavam belongs to Telangana (a common confusion with AP). Madhya Pradesh's central tribal tradition includes Karma dance, an entirely distinct form.

questions.stem: Among the three forms of Bihu celebrated in Assam, which one marks the end of the harvesting season and is associated with communal feasting and bonfires called 'Meji'?

options.option_text: Bhogali Bihu, the winter harvest festival held in January
Rongali Bihu, the spring new year festival in April month
Kongali Bihu, the sombre autumn festival of oil lamps
Bordoisila Bihu, a special variant for young unmarried women

questions.explanation: Bhogali Bihu (Magh Bihu, January) celebrates harvest completion with feasting and Meji bonfires. Rongali Bihu (Bohag Bihu, April) is the most exuberant form, marking the Assamese New Year. Kongali Bihu (Kati Bihu, October) is sombre — lamps are lit in lean fields. 'Bordoisila' is a spring wind referenced in Assamese folk songs, not a separate Bihu category — a classic distractor in exams.

questions.stem: Among the major variants of Chhau dance recognised by UNESCO, which form is performed entirely WITHOUT masks, relying solely on facial expressions and body language?

options.option_text: Purulia Chhau from West Bengal, known for ornate temple masks
Dalma Chhau, a variant associated with the Jharkhand plateau
Seraikella Chhau from Jharkhand, noted for refined elegant masks
Mayurbhanj Chhau from northern Odisha, performed without masks

questions.explanation: Mayurbhanj Chhau (from Baripada, northern Odisha) is the only recognised Chhau form that uses no masks — performers convey emotion through body movement and facial expression alone. Purulia Chhau (West Bengal) uses brilliant, colourful masks depicting deities and demons. Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand) also uses masks, though of a more refined, stylised variety. 'Dalma Chhau' is not a recognised form — Dalma is a hill range in Jharkhand, inserted here as a plausible geographic distractor.

questions.stem: The Nati dance of Himachal Pradesh earned a Guinness World Record. Which specific feat earned it this distinction?

options.option_text: Largest number of participants in a single folk dance event
Highest altitude folk dance performed at over 5,000 metres
Fastest footwork tempo recorded in any traditional dance form
Oldest uninterrupted dance tradition documented in South Asia

questions.explanation: In 2016, approximately 10,578 participants performed the Nati dance simultaneously at Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, setting the Guinness World Record for the largest folk dance by participant count. Nati is a slow, graceful chain dance performed during melas (fairs) and festivals in the Kullu-Shimla belt. None of the other options correspond to any recorded Guinness achievement for Nati or any Indian folk dance form.

questions.stem: The Karma dance, performed as worship of the Karma tree (Nauclea parvifolia) during the Karma Puja festival, is primarily associated with tribal communities of which region?

options.option_text: Warli and Bhil tribes of Maharashtra and Gujarat region
Tribal communities across Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and MP
Toda and Irula tribes of the Nilgiris range in Tamil Nadu
Khasi and Garo tribes of the northeastern hill states region

questions.explanation: Karma Puja and its associated dance are observed across the central Indian tribal belt — by communities including the Oraon, Munda, Ho, Baiga, and Gond — spanning Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Madhya Pradesh. The Karma tree is worshipped as a symbol of prosperity and youthful vitality. The Khasi-Garo communities (Meghalaya) and Toda-Irula communities (Nilgiris) follow entirely distinct ritual dance traditions unrelated to Karma Puja.

questions.stem: The Nongkrem dance, a five-day ritualistic festival of Meghalaya's Khasi tribe, is performed by young women in silk attire to propitiate which deity?

options.option_text: U Ryngkew Basa, the guardian spirit of Khasi households
Ka Blei Synshar, the supreme divine being of Khasi belief
Ka Mei Ramew, the Earth Mother goddess of the Jaintia hills
U Lum Sohpetbneng, venerated as the sacred navel of the earth

questions.explanation: Nongkrem is performed annually at Smit village in the Khasi Hills to thank Ka Blei Synshar — the Almighty God in Niam Khasi, the indigenous Khasi religion. Young women dance in silk skirts and silver ornaments alongside male warriors. U Ryngkew Basa is a domestic-protective clan deity (a genuine distractor since 'Basa' implies household association). Ka Mei Ramew is the Khasi Earth Mother concept, and U Lum Sohpetbneng is a sacred peak in Khasi cosmology — all authentic Khasi spiritual concepts inserted as expert-level traps.

questions.stem: The Ojapali tradition of Assam has two streams: one narrates episodes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata. What is the second stream and to which deity is it dedicated?

options.option_text: Byah Ojapali, dedicated to the god Vishnu and his consort
Gosain Ojapali, a Neo-Vaishnavite form from the Majuli sattras
Maroi Ojapali, dedicated to Manasha, the serpent goddess
Bihu Ojapali, performed to please the river goddess Dihing

questions.explanation: Ojapali comprises two streams: Sukananni Ojapali, which glorifies Vishnu and narrates episodes from the epics, and Maroi Ojapali (Maroi Deva Ojapali), which propitiates Manasha, the serpent goddess. The lead Oja narrates through song and gesture while Palis provide the chorus. 'Gosain Ojapali' is a plausible distractor — 'Gosain' is associated with Vaishnavite traditions and Majuli sattras are real centres of Assamese culture — but no such formal Ojapali stream exists. 'Byah' (wedding) and 'Bihu' Ojapali are entirely fictional variants.
